intro: くらい (also ぐらい; both are correct and mean the same) is a rough measure: "about that much". After a number it blurs an amount; after a clause or noun it sets a degree, either high ("so ... that") or low ("at least this much").

skills.rule: [amount] くらい means "about [amount]": use it for quantities and durations, ごろ for points in time.
skills.explain:
Put くらい after a number and counter to make it approximate: 一時間くらい, 二十人くらい, 三千円ぐらい. どのくらい asks "how much / how long". It is the everyday word for "about"; ほど means the same but sounds more formal.

A duration is not a point in time, so it takes no に: 二時間くらい勉強しました. Frequency works the same way: 一週間に三回くらい.

For a point on the clock or calendar the standard word is ごろ: 三時ごろ. In casual speech people also say 三時くらいに, but the reverse never works: ごろ cannot follow an amount, so 一時間ごろ is wrong. だけ ("only") and まで ("up to / until") set limits rather than estimates.

examples.jp: 一時間[いちじかん]{くらい}勉強[べんきょう]しました。
examples.en: I studied for about an hour.

examples.jp: このかばんは三千円[さんぜんえん]{ぐらい}でした。
examples.en: This bag was about three thousand yen.

examples.jp: 教室[きょうしつ]に学生[がくせい]が二十人[にじゅうにん]{くらい}います。
examples.en: There are about twenty students in the classroom.

examples.jp: 東京[とうきょう]から大阪[おおさか]まで、どの{くらい}かかりますか。
examples.en: How long does it take from Tokyo to Osaka?

examples.jp: 一週間[いっしゅうかん]に三回[さんかい]{くらい}泳[およ]ぎます。
examples.en: I swim about three times a week.

contrast.note: ごろ blurs a point in time (三時ごろ, "around three"); くらい blurs an amount (三時間くらい, "about three hours").
Same meaning after an amount, but more formal. どのくらい has no ほど version; use どれほど.
だけ is "only": 一時間だけ sets a limit, 一時間くらい gives an estimate.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]で一時間[いちじかん]{ごろ}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]で一時間[いちじかん]{くらい}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.note: An hour is an amount of time, not a point on the clock, so it takes くらい.

mistakes.bad: 二時間[にじかん]くらい{に}勉強[べんきょう]しました。
mistakes.good: 二時間[にじかん]{くらい}勉強[べんきょう]しました。
mistakes.note: A duration takes no に, with or without くらい.

skills.tip: Is it an amount you could count (hours, people, yen, times)? くらい. A moment on the clock or calendar? ごろ.

skills.rule: Xくらい sets a degree: after a clause it means "so ... that X"; after a small noun it means "at least X" or "that little".
skills.explain:
After a plain verb or adjective, くらい names a result to show how far something goes: 歩けないくらい足が痛い, "my feet hurt so much I can't walk". Here ほど works equally well.

At the low end, くらい marks the minimum you would expect: 挨拶くらいしてください, "at least say hello"; それくらい自分でできる, "I can do that much myself". This belittling sense belongs to くらい alone; ほど cannot carry it. It often appears in reproaches and in ～くらいは ("at least").

With a noun and a negative, it means "nobody / nothing as ... as": 田中さんくらい料理が上手な人はいない. だけ means "only" and まで means "even" or "until", so swapping them in changes the sentence. しか needs a negative verb and means "nothing but".
patterns: [plain verb / adjective] くらい [adjective / verb]  "so ... that"
[noun] くらい [adjective] 人 / もの は いない / ない

examples.jp: それ{くらい}自分[じぶん]でできるよ。
examples.en: I can do that much myself.

examples.jp: 挨拶[あいさつ]{くらい}してください。
歩[ある]けない{くらい}足[あし]が痛[いた]いです。
examples.en: My feet hurt so much I can't walk.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]は眠[ねむ]れない{くらい}暑[あつ]かった。
examples.en: Last night was so hot I couldn't sleep.

examples.jp: 遅[おく]れるなら、電話[でんわ]{くらい}してくれればよかったのに。
examples.en: If you were going to be late, you could at least have called.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さん{くらい}料理[りょうり]が上手[じょうず]な人[ひと]はいません。
examples.en: Nobody cooks as well as Ms Tanaka.

contrast.note: Both work for "so ... that" (歩けないほど / くらい). Only くらい works for the low "at least / that little" sense.
挨拶だけして is "just say hello (and nothing else)"; 挨拶くらいして is "at least say hello".
しか needs a negative and means "nothing but": 水しか飲まない. くらい sets a minimum, not an exclusive limit.

mistakes.bad: 挨拶[あいさつ]{ほど}してください。
mistakes.good: 挨拶[あいさつ]{くらい}してください。
mistakes.note: "At least" is a low degree; ほど cannot mark it.

mistakes.bad: 歩[ある]けない{まで}足[あし]が痛[いた]いです。
mistakes.good: 歩[ある]けない{くらい}足[あし]が痛[いた]いです。
mistakes.note: まで is "until"; the degree of pain is くらい (or ほど).

skills.tip: English "so ... that" or "at least"? くらい. If it is "at least", ほど is out.
